purpose: Learn transferable mechanisms behind durable global products and organizations, then translate them into IMA without copying surface features or harmful incentives.
canonical_question: What human behavior, product architecture, distribution mechanism, experience, business model, timing advantage, ecosystem effect, or cultural meaning made this successful—and what is the humane IMA equivalent?

reference_families.name: Apple / iPhone
lessons: Replace a fragmented category with a simpler end-to-end experience.
Combine existing technologies into a coherent new product rather than requiring users to understand the technology.
Use interaction design as a breakthrough: direct manipulation, low learning cost, immediate feedback.
Integrate hardware, software, services, distribution and support so the whole experience feels like one product.
Turn the product into a platform so third parties can create unexpected value.
Build a recognizable identity and quality bar that makes the product culturally legible.
Expand from one breakthrough into an ecosystem of adjacent products and services.
Scale globally while preserving a consistent core experience and adapting language, regulation and distribution locally.
ima_equivalent: IMA must feel like one system, not a collection of AI tools.
Make the first interaction immediately understandable and useful.
Unify intelligence, memory, creation, tools, community, devices and experiences behind one human-centered layer.
Create an open IMA ecosystem where creators, professionals, organizations and developers can add value.
Build trust, accessibility, beauty and reliability into the core rather than as add-ons.
Expand IMA across web, mobile, desktop, wearables, vehicles, robots, AR/VR and future interfaces without losing the human-centered core.

reference_families.name: Rockstar / GTA
lessons: Create a world people can enter, not merely a feature list.
Give users meaningful freedom inside clear rules.
Use missions and progression to turn a large world into actionable experiences.
Combine solo depth with persistent online participation.
Release substantial updates that reactivate an established world.
Make the world culturally memorable through characters, places, stories, music and user-created moments.
Build long-lived economics around ongoing value.
ima_equivalent: IMA should be a coherent living world of knowledge, creation, exploration and human connection.
Offer missions, play, discovery, creation, stories, music and collaboration as user-chosen experiences.
Preserve authorized continuity across sessions and devices.
Create recurring reasons to return through genuinely new value, not compulsion.
Let users become contributors and creators inside the IMA world.
Monetize experiences, professional capabilities and services only after verified value.

reference_families.name: Platform winners
lessons: Solve the two-sided or multi-sided ecosystem problem: users need value and creators need users.
Distribution is part of the product.
Network effects become powerful only after the core experience is strong enough to attract the first participants.
Standards, APIs, tooling and documentation can turn a product into infrastructure.
ima_equivalent: IMA must serve people first while making it easy for creators, businesses, educators, researchers and developers to build useful things on top.
Treat distribution, localization, accessibility and discoverability as product features.
Build interoperable interfaces and a trustworthy contribution model.

reference_families.name: Durable global organizations
lessons: Strong brands repeatedly deliver a recognizable promise.
Operational excellence turns a good idea into a repeatable global experience.
Feedback loops and measurement prevent growth from becoming self-deception.
Successful organizations adapt while preserving a clear core identity.
The strongest products often create a category or redefine what users expect from an existing category.
ima_equivalent: IMA should define and repeatedly deliver a clear promise: human-centered intelligence that increases human capability and agency.
Run one loop across product, engineering, QA, research, community, distribution, accessibility, partnerships and economics.
Continuously search for category-defining simplifications and experiences.

innovation_rules: Do not copy surface features; copy transferable mechanisms.
Prefer category creation or category redefinition over feature accumulation.
Every major feature must answer: what human problem becomes easier, better, more beautiful or more possible?
Experience is a legitimate product value; enjoyment, curiosity, play, creation and wonder count as outcomes.
Retention is a consequence of value and experience, never the primary target.
Do not optimize time spent, streaks, compulsion, fear of missing out, or dependency as ends in themselves.
The user can leave, export, understand and control their data and progress.
Globalization means a common core plus local language, culture, accessibility and regulatory adaptation.
IMA should continuously study successful products, failed products and emerging products and translate the underlying lessons into experiments.

global_breakthrough_goal.north_star: Make IMA a globally recognizable human-centered intelligence experience that people choose because it makes life, work, learning and creation more possible—and because the experience itself is worth returning to.

phases.name: CORE_BREAKTHROUGH
phases.exit: A new user can understand IMA and reach a useful or enjoyable outcome quickly.

phases.name: LIVING_WORLD
phases.exit: Practical help and optional experiences feel like one coherent IMA world.

phases.name: GLOBAL_PRODUCT
phases.exit: Core journeys work reliably across priority languages, devices and accessibility needs.

phases.name: ECOSYSTEM
phases.exit: External creators, professionals, organizations and developers can create verified value through IMA.

phases.name: CULTURE
phases.exit: Users voluntarily create, share and teach things that make IMA culturally useful and recognizable.

phases.name: SUSTAINABLE_SCALE
phases.exit: Revenue grows from demonstrated value without compromising human agency or trust.

operating_requirements: Every release must improve a measured user outcome or remove a major category friction.
Every week identify the highest-leverage gap preventing global adoption and ship or instrument the smallest credible fix.
Every major product decision must be evaluated against the universal innovation loop.
Do not declare global success from traffic, impressions, followers or synthetic signals.
When evidence is missing, mark UNKNOWN and create the measurement needed.
Treat reliability, accessibility, localization, trust and onboarding as growth features.
Continuously benchmark successful and failed products without copying their surface design.
